definition: A tendency for evaluators (human or AI) to favor longer responses, independent of their actual quality or correctness.
details: Length bias is a recognized confound in both human evaluation and LLM-as-a-judge setups, motivating evaluation methodologies that explicitly control for or normalize against response length.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. In plain words: A tendency for evaluators (human or AI) to favor longer responses, independent of their actual quality or correctness. Here is how it actually plays out: Length bias is a recognized confound in both human evaluation and LLM-as-a-judge setups, motivating evaluation methodologies that explicitly control for or normalize against response length. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Length Bias (in evaluation).
